title: Adaptive intake form and SLA-based routing tree for enterprise data-control requests
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Context:
Enterprise customers regularly submit non-bug data-control requests (logging redaction, retention policy changes, PII handling, audit exports). Current intake is a single generic form routed to a shared triage inbox which causes long TTV, incorrect routing, and inconsistent SLAs.

Problem statement:
- High friction for customers to describe regulatory deadlines and technical constraints.
- Triage team spends 40% of cycles clarifying scope instead of delivering.
- Missing standard priority signals (regulatory deadline, production impact, data volume) cause unpredictable routing.

Goal:
Design and implement an adaptive intake form plus a decision matrix that: (1) collects structured signals to compute a routed priority score, (2) maps requests to an SLA tier and owner queue (Support, Solutions Eng, Legal ops, Eng on-call), and (3) surfaces required artifacts and expedited response templates. Target: reduce time-to-first-meaningful-response to under 48 hours for high-impact enterprise requests.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Adaptive Intake Form (Console + Public Intake): dynamic branching questions that reveal additional fields based on answers (e.g., regulatory region -> ask for regulation name + deadline; PII yes -> ask schema + sample rows).
2) Weighted Decision Matrix: compute a 0-100 priority score from four weighted factors: Compliance urgency (35%), Production impact (30%), Technical complexity/risk (20%), Customer tier / contract SLA (15%).
3) SLA Routing Tree: map score thresholds to queues and SLA targets: 80-100 -> Expedited (24h TTFR) -> Legal+SE+Eng on-call; 60-79 -> High (48h TTFR) -> Solutions Eng + Support; 30-59 -> Medium (5 business days) -> Support; <30 -> Backlog / PM review.
4) Required artifact checklist: for high scores the form will require attachments (audit log samples, retention policies, internal contact). Missing artifacts flag request as 'info needed' and auto-schedule clarifying follow-up.
5) Response templates & playbooks: pre-written customer-facing templates, internal runbook links, and assignment rules.

Decision matrix (example calculation):
- Compliance urgency: none=0, advisory=10, compliance window>90d=20, <90d=60, immediate/regulatory action=100.
- Production impact: none=0, minor=20, user-facing degradation=60, data loss/incident=100.
- Technical complexity: trivial=0, moderate=40, requires infra changes=80, on-prem/VPC constraints=90.
- Customer tier: Free=0, Startup=10, Business=30, Enterprise=60.
Score = round(0.35*Compliance + 0.30*Impact + 0.20*Complexity + 0.15*Tier).

Intake sample fields (adaptive):
- Request type (Logging redaction | Retention change | PII handling | Audit export | Other)
- Customer tier & contract reference
- Region(s) impacted and legal jurisdiction
- Is this tied to an external regulatory deadline? If yes: deadline date, regulation name, evidence link
- Data categories affected (PII, financial, health, other) + schema sample (optional attachment)
- Data volume and retention currently in place
- Desired outcome (e.g., redact past logs, purge records, create export endpoint)
- Business impact description and number of affected customers
- Required artifacts (checkboxes populated dynamically)

Routing targets and owners (examples):
- Expedited (score >=80): Legal Ops (lead), Solutions Engineering (implementation owner), Eng on-call for infra changes.
- High (60-79): Solutions Engineering (owner) + CS Tier 2.
- Medium (30-59): Support Tier 1, PM review for product changes.
- Low (<30): PM backlog; quarterly grouping for product roadmap if recurring.

Acceptance criteria (must be met to consider ticket done):
- Adaptive form available in Console + public intake page with branching behavior and required attachments enforced for high/expedited flows.
- Priority score computed and visible in ticket header.
- Incoming requests with score >=80 auto-create an incident-style triage in internal queue and notify Legal+SE+Eng on-call.
- Templates for customer responses for each SLA tier are created and vetted by Legal.
- Telemetry: time-to-first-meaningful-response, percent blocked-for-info, average score distribution, per-team SLA compliance; dashboards in Console available to PM and Support leads.

Telemetry and QA:
- Track the following events: form_started, form_completed, score_computed, routed_to_queue, attachment_uploaded, ttf_response.
- Create a dashboard with heatmap by region and common request types to identify automation opportunities (e.g., retention policy presets).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How strict should artifact enforcement be for expedited paths? (blocking submission vs. post-routing required)
- Do we create a separate public intake endpoint for regulated customers to preserve PII handling?
- Reuse existing ticketing IDs (Support) vs. create new 'Data Control Requests' queue in Linear.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 1 (2 sprints): Mockups + backend scoring engine + basic branching + routing to manual inbox for high scores.
- Phase 2 (next 2 sprints): Auto-routing + notifications + templates + dashboards.
- Phase 3 (Q2): Integrations with Dedicated/Private support orgs, audit logs, and retention policy automation.
updates: 2026-03-01 - Created ticket and initial proposal. Linked to project charter in Confluence.
2026-03-03 - PM sync with Support: confirmed average clarifying back-and-forth is ~2.1 comments per ticket. Support prefers required artifact prompts for >=60 score.
2026-03-05 - Engineering scoping: backend scoring engine estimated 3 days of backend work + 2 days for backend-to-linear routing; design to provide field-level rules.
2026-03-07 - Design review: low-fidelity mockups approved with inline help text and example phrasings for legal-sensitive fields.

2026-03-09 - Security review requested: added checkbox for encrypted attachments and recommended S3 pre-signed URL pattern for uploads. Security raised requirement for opt-in PII redaction when attachments are stored in long-term buckets.

2026-03-12 - Decision: adopt blocking artifact enforcement only for 'Expedited' (>=80) and 'High' (60-79) when regulatory deadline is within 90 days. Next: ENG to start implementation of scoring service and routing hooks.
comments: Support (Asha Patel): 'If we can push required minimal artifacts in form, ops time for clarifying drops significantly. We should include a 'copy to CSM' checkbox.'
Security (Rahul Mehta): 'Attachments must be scanned for PII and stored encrypted. Consider ephemeral storage when customer selects 'redact request' option.'
Legal (Marta Ruiz): 'Response templates need legal approval. For regulatory deadlines we will need a dedicated SLA that includes Legal Ops review step.'
Engineering (Nora Kim): 'Backend scoring microservice will be reusable for other intake types (feature requests). Estimate bumped if we need historical ticket signal enrichment.'
Design (Evan Lowe): 'Adding progressive disclosure for optional schema upload reduces cognitive load. We'll provide microcopy examples.'
